weaknesses: The proposal treats the free slot after physiotherapy as mostly usable work capacity, but Monday has Posture Physiotherapy from 11:00 to 12:30 followed by only a 30-minute gap before Video Editing from 13:00 to 18:30. That may be workable for some people, but the rationale does not substantiate that this is enough time for lunch, transition, recovery, or resetting after a medical therapy session.

The moved Monday editing block is longer than the explicitly mentioned prior option of 13:30-18:00, increasing Monday's focused work demand before a Live Stream from 20:00 to 23:30. The proposal explains the productivity benefit, but gives limited attention to the cost of concentrating a longer cognitive block after therapy and before evening performance work.

Across the visible week, the routine is already demanding: Tuesday through Friday each include Sleep until 09:30, Gym Workout from 10:00 to 11:30, Video Editing from 12:30 to 18:00, and Live Stream from 20:00 to 23:30. This appears largely pre-existing and should not automatically be blamed on the proposed change, but the Monday extension adds load into an already dense visible pattern without discussing cumulative sustainability.

The alternatives considered are relevant but narrow. They compare keeping the old editing time, starting immediately after physiotherapy, or adding work after the stream, but they do not show whether a less compressed or less extended Monday option was considered within the visible flexibility.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The proposal is technically coherent and preserves the fixed health and sleep blocks, and the stated 30-minute post-therapy buffer is better than starting editing immediately at 12:30. However, the human-quality case is only partially supported. The resulting Monday has physiotherapy from 11:00 to 12:30, then a 5.5-hour editing block from 13:00 to 18:30, then a live stream from 20:00 to 23:30. In isolation this may be possible, but it leaves little visibly protected margin after therapy and creates a long cognitive-production day. Over the visible horizon, the following days repeat gym, editing, streaming, and late sleep timing, so the added Monday load deserves more justification than simply saying the slot is free. Because the original request is not provided, request satisfaction cannot be verified; the review can only assess whether the visible plan looks realistically manageable.

plausibility_review.reason: The proposed move could materially affect manageability by extending Monday editing to 13:00-18:30 after a fixed physiotherapy session ending at 12:30 and before a 20:00-23:30 live stream. The concern is not an objective conflict: the events fit, and the user may tolerate this pattern. The issue is that the rationale does not adequately address recovery, food, transition, and cumulative fatigue in a week that already contains repeated long editing and streaming days.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider or better substantiate the Monday distribution using the proposer’s fuller context: explain why the 30-minute post-therapy margin and longer editing block are realistically sustainable, or consider a less compressed way to protect video-production time without assuming all free calendar time after therapy is effective work capacity.

weaknesses: The revision meaningfully improves the prior post-physiotherapy concern by moving the main Monday editing block to 13:30-18:30, leaving a 1-hour gap after Posture Physiotherapy ends at 12:30. However, it partly shifts the pressure to the morning: Sleep ends at 09:30, Video Editing Prep is scheduled 10:00-10:30, and physiotherapy starts at 11:00. That leaves only visible 30-minute margins on either side of the prep block for waking routines, food, travel or setup, none of which are shown.

Monday remains a dense production-and-performance day: Video Editing Prep from 10:00-10:30, Posture Physiotherapy from 11:00-12:30, Video Editing from 13:30-18:30, and Live Stream from 20:00-23:30. The plan is plausible, but still depends on the user being able to recover from therapy and sustain focused editing plus evening streaming on the same day.

The visible week remains cumulatively demanding, with Tuesday through Friday each showing Gym Workout from 10:00-11:30, Video Editing from 12:30-18:00, and Live Stream from 20:00-23:30 after Sleep ending at 09:30. This is mostly pre-existing and should not be blamed on the revision, but the rationale could more explicitly explain why Monday should match the weekday video-production pattern rather than leaving extra recovery margin around the medical session.

The rationale considers relevant alternatives and directly responds to the previous concern about a too-short post-therapy transition, but it still does not substantiate the practical morning feasibility of the added 10:00-10:30 prep block beyond noting that travel, meals, hygiene and recovery are not shown.
critic_evaluation.feedback: This revised proposal is more humanly plausible than the prior version. The main improvement is that the editing block no longer starts at 13:00 after physiotherapy; it starts at 13:30, preserving a more credible post-therapy transition. Splitting the video-production workload into a short 10:00-10:30 prep block and a 13:30-18:30 main block also avoids placing more work after the 20:00-23:30 stream or near protected sleep. The remaining concern is not a clear failure, but a practical dependency: the new prep block compresses the morning between Sleep ending at 09:30 and Posture Physiotherapy at 11:00, and the calendar does not show whether the user needs travel, breakfast, hygiene, setup, or other preparation before therapy. Because the revised plan addresses the prior post-therapy compression and no stronger supported alternative is visible from the provided scope, another revision is not required on human-quality grounds. The proposer should, however, verify or explain the morning practicality and the user’s tolerance for a therapy-plus-production-plus-stream Monday.

plausibility_review.reason: The prior material concern about a 30-minute post-physiotherapy gap has been substantially addressed: the main editing block now starts at 13:30 after physiotherapy ends at 12:30. The added 10:00-10:30 prep block introduces a new morning-compression uncertainty between Sleep ending at 09:30 and physiotherapy starting at 11:00, but the impact is limited to a short block and the rationale acknowledges that practical needs are not shown. There is no demonstrated contradiction or sufficiently concrete evidence that the resulting Monday is unmanageable.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Keep the current distribution only if the proposer’s fuller context supports that the 10:00-10:30 prep block is realistic before physiotherapy. If not, reconsider the distribution generally to preserve morning preparation, food, travel or therapy-readiness margin without relying on all visible free time being usable work capacity.
